Technical / Requirements details (copied from meetings, paraphrased):
- Workloads: interactive chat (low-latency, streaming), offline summarization (high-throughput batched tokens), reranking for search (tight latency for top-K).
- Latency SLO targets: interactive p95 <= 180ms tokenized (streaming enabled), p99 <= 400ms; search rerank p95 <= 120ms. Nightly summarization throughput target: sustain average 250k tokens/sec across pool during batch windows.
- Availability/SLA: target 99.95% for production endpoints; request clear credit schedule and priority response (1-hour P1).
- Reserved GPU planning: initial conservative pool: 8x H100-80GB equiv for model variants with burst-to-shared capacity for peak hour; finance prefers A100 for cost reasons — need TCO comparison.
- Model preferences: customer will use a mix of open LLMs fine-tuned on clinical data; must support 32k context (30k typical). Also evaluating Redwood-verified LLMs with medically-aligned safety filters.
- Quantization profile ask: test nf4/4-bit quant vs 8-bit to measure throughput vs hallucination/regression impact. ML lead wants baseline quality with int8, then evaluate nf4-4bit for dedicated runtime to halve memory footprint.
- Batching / KV cache: prefer persistent KV cache for active chat sessions; plan to pin cache to dedicated pool instances with warmup policy. Target continuous-batching for summarization jobs; max batch latency budget 100ms for reranking traffic.
- Fallback/routing: require automated fallback to smaller model variant when full pool is degraded; must preserve PHI restrictions (no fallback to hosted multi-tenant unless private VPC option enabled).

POC scope agreed:
- Run two model families (clinical-optimized 32k-context, and compact 8k-context) across three quant profiles (fp16 baseline, int8, nf4-4bit) on a 4-node H100-equivalent Dedicated cluster. Measure p50/p95/p99 latency for streaming tokens and batch throughput for summarization.
